title: Read-Only Candidate Inspection And Writer Lifetime
summary: P3B distinguishes durable preparation history from an explicitly observed candidate, without activating, deleting, repairing or releasing reservations.

api.request: No query parameters or client paths. Authentication and project-scoped DB lookup precede all route and artifact access. Missing and denied jobs both return 404.
api.response: The normal shin.server-response.v1 envelope contains shin.preparation-inspection.v1. HTTP 200 means an observation was returned, not that the candidate is verified.
api.admission: At most one prepared-candidate inspection per server process. A concurrent inspection receives 503/preparation-inspection-busy, not an unbounded wait or extra artifact load. Non-prepared rows return without filesystem access.
api.availability: Inspection is available even when new preparation jobs are disabled. Execution fingerprint and existing private artifact namespace must still match.

result.job: Unchanged public historical ledger row; no worker id, lease, principal id, request hash or artifact filesystem path.
result.observation: scope=candidate-observation, started_at and finished_at in server UTC. This is an observation interval, not an atomic worktree snapshot, signed receipt, deployment proof or reusable currentness token.

checks.route: matched / changed / unavailable / not-assessed: configured execution fingerprint, registered project identity, profile bytes and private state identity.
checks.writer: quiescent / busy / unavailable / not-assessed: shared nonblocking lifetime lock excludes cooperating writers only while inspection owns it.
checks.artifact: verified / missing / invalid / not-assessed: exact generated layout, no symbolic/hard links or unknown entries, bounded immutable Core snapshot load and manifest integrity.
checks.ledger: matched / mismatch / unavailable / not-assessed: loaded snapshot id and payload bytes agree with the prepared row; the input row is rechecked at completion.
checks.doctor: passed / failed / unavailable / not-assessed: current invocation of the existing strict Core safety/consistency inspection. This is not eval or Pack acceptance.
checks.source: current / drifted / unavailable / not-assessed: exact Core regenerated-output comparison, not cached metadata or an Observer notification.
checks.base: matched / changed / unavailable / not-assessed: DB active-route revision and snapshot identity equal the enqueue precondition before and after verification. Identity alone does not certify the active artifact's integrity.

result.candidate_verified: True only when all seven checks pass in this request. Non-prepared jobs report candidate-not-prepared. A retention intent or released ledger returns candidate-retention-pending or candidate-released, without accessing the candidate. Historical prepared status never overrides this boundary.
result.negativeEvidence: reason_codes retain bounded stable codes, not raw exceptions, secret-like content or local paths. A failed later check does not erase the explicitly scoped earlier observations.
result.notActivation: activation_supported=true and activation_ready=false even on success. Ordinary inspection does not run quality suites, create a receipt or authorize publication; preparation plus Doctor is not all project quality gates.
result.nonMutation: mutations_performed=false. No DB update/audit event, mkdir, lock creation, repair, expiry, cancellation, deletion, quota release, active publication or source write. Operating-system read access metadata is not a publication.

writerLifetime.layout: Each claimed worker creates state_dir/.job-<id>-<artifact_key>.lock exclusively, mode 0600, and holds flock(LOCK_EX) through all candidate IO and the prepared DB transition. Namespace/key binding is persisted and separate from the internal Core publication/writer locks.
writerLifetime.inspection: Open the existing empty owner-private regular lock with O_NOFOLLOW, O_NONBLOCK and O_CLOEXEC; require one hard link and acquire flock(LOCK_SH|LOCK_NB). Verify the named inode against the held descriptor before and after observation.
writerLifetime.retention: Never unlink the lifetime lock in a destructor. A descriptor-owning process can survive lease expiry or database recovery; PostgreSQL state alone is not writer quiescence.
writerLifetime.crash: The kernel releases the descriptor lock after the process exits. The file remains as stable lock identity. Missing, replaced or unsafe lock state fails closed; inspection never creates a replacement.
writerLifetime.deploymentBoundary: Local filesystem and cooperating same-host server processes. Not a security sandbox against a malicious same-UID process, not distributed fencing, and not certified on NFS/SMB. Old candidate execution fingerprints are not silently reinterpreted by a new development version.

resourceBounds.payload: One inspection may retain at most retrieval.max_generation_bytes in immutable candidate bytes, with per-file limits. This is additional to the retrieval cache and preparation worker; it is not a total process RSS cap.
resourceBounds.work: Fixed generated layout bounds directory inventory. Exact freshness still regenerates profile-bounded output; transient parsing/generation memory is separate from resident payload. No warm-currentness shortcut was introduced.
resourceBounds.waiting: Lifetime lock acquisition is nonblocking. Existing Core publication locks and source processing retain their documented cooperative waits; no hard inspection deadline is claimed.

sources.use: Descriptor lifetime, independent opens, advisory and nonblocking semantics; remote filesystem limitations.
Local Darwin shared/exclusive advisory file locking; it does not stop an uncooperative process.
